narrative.overview:
Helium looks like a lab bench at night, with an ice core under dark-field light that you read one layer at a time. The ground is polar-night navy and the type is frost white. The only warm light in the room is helium peach, the glow of a discharge tube, and it falls on whatever is current. Other states get a physical mark instead of a hue: a strip of tape for the value in force, a strike through the value it replaced, a folded flag for work that needs review, and a dashed pencil outline for a draft nobody has sent. Evidence comes out of the dark onto cool-white light-table sheets. It is set in ink, and the words people actually said are set in Spectral italic.

One world runs at two densities. The public entrance is spacious and cinematic. It has expanded Archivo display type up to 6rem, a single orchestrated scroll drill through a WebGL core, and sections separated by hairlines that alternate between two navy tones. The workspace is a dense tool for operators: a 56px header, a sticky core rail on the left, a 30rem drawer on the right, segmented tabs, and rows of facts at about 0.92 to 0.98rem. Both share every token, mark and control.

The build overrides the direction contract (`.impeccable/surfaces/apps-site-app-page-tsx.md`). The contract still describes a deep slate-teal ground and a helium-yellow D3 line. The user rejected that first palette, and the shipped build replaced it with navy and peach. This file records the build. The confirmed visual rejections are the replaced teal-and-yellow palette and anything that resembles Minutes, the upstream prototype: paper white with cobalt, Cal Sans or Manrope, a nine-tile block mark, or isometric block sculpture.
keyCharacteristics: Polar-night navy ground in five tonal steps. There is no light mode.
One warm colour, peach, reserved for "current": the value in force, the date cut, the active location and the primary action.
State is always shown as a mark plus words, never by colour alone.
Evidence sits on cool-white sheets with ink text. Everything else stays dark.
One sans family (Archivo) driven across its width axis. Spectral italic is only for people's words, and JetBrains Mono is only for Cypher and IDs.
Tight corners (1 to 3px), frost hairlines, flat resting surfaces, and a 5% film grain over the whole page.
Sentence case throughout. No uppercase labels.
Every animated or 3D surface has a reduced-motion path and a fallback that works without WebGL.

rules.name: The Peach Is Now Rule
rules.body: Peach means current: the value in force, the date being read, the place you are, and the one action to take next. It is never a category colour or a second accent, and it fills at most one button in any group of controls.

rules.name: The Mark, Not Hue Rule
rules.body: Every state shows a physical mark and a word. "In force" gets tape, "Superseded" gets a strike, "Needs review" gets a folded flag, and "Unsent draft" gets a dashed pencil outline. Screen-reader text names the state wherever the word is not visible.

rules.name: The Light Table Rule
rules.body: Light surfaces are reserved for things a person reads as evidence: source quotes and emails, the belief-at-a-date table, and drafted notes. Inside a sheet, selection inverts to ink on sheet. Everything else stays on the navy field.

rules.name: The Width Axis Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy comes from Archivo's width axis as much as from size. Use expanded widths (wdth 104 to 118) at heavy weights for display, titles, values and the wordmark. Use normal width (100) for prose and controls. Use condensed widths (86 to 92) for labels, dates, rail readouts and drawer titles. Never introduce a second sans.

rules.name: The Human Words Rule
rules.body: Spectral italic is only for words a person said or wrote, and JetBrains Mono is only for Cypher and IDs. Neither one appears on headings, buttons or navigation.

rules.name: The Tabular Time Rule
rules.body: Every date, count, timing and depth uses tabular numerals, so values that change in place, like the date cut or the rail readout, don't jitter.

rules.name: The Floating-Only Rule
rules.body: Resting surfaces carry no shadow: sections, cards, rows, fields and disclosures. A shadow appears only on something that floats (the nav bar, popovers, tooltips, the cut readout) or on a sheet lifted out to be read.

rules.name: The Dashed Means Not Yet Rule
rules.body: A dashed outline marks anything provisional or absent: an unsent draft, the offline-sample source badge, an empty state, the "no receipt" panel, a value not yet said on the light table, and the future remainder of a live value. A solid border means the thing exists in the record.

dos: Do keep Helium Peach (#ffae8a) for what is current: the value in force, the date cut, the active location and the single primary action in a group.
Do pair every state with its mark and its word: tape for "In force", a strike for "Superseded", a folded flag for "Needs review", and a dashed pencil outline for "Unsent draft".
Do put source quotes, emails, belief readings and drafted notes on the Light Table sheet (#f3f6fa) in Ink, with the sheet-lift shadow.
Do separate resting surfaces with frost hairlines (rgb(148 176 214 / 0.14)) and navy tone steps, not shadows.
Do set dates, counts, timings and depths in tabular numerals, and use condensed Archivo (wdth 86 to 92) for rail readouts and labels.
Do use a dashed outline for anything provisional, offline, empty or not yet said.
Do give every scroll-driven, animated or WebGL surface a `prefers-reduced-motion` path and a static or SVG fallback.
donts: Don't let anything resemble Minutes: no paper-white with cobalt (#3155ed), no Cal Sans or Manrope, no nine-tile block mark, and no isometric block sculpture.
Don't return to the replaced first palette of a slate-teal ground with helium or mustard yellow. The user rejected it in favour of navy and peach.
Don't use peach as a category colour, a second accent or a decorative fill, and don't put two solid peach buttons side by side.
Don't show state by colour alone.
Don't set headings, buttons or navigation in Spectral or JetBrains Mono, or prose in mono.
Don't add shadows to resting cards, rows or sections, and never use hard offset shadows.
Don't round resting controls or cards beyond 3px, or make pill-shaped buttons. 6px belongs only to the floating nav and the screenshot frame.
Don't open sections with uppercase tracked eyebrow labels. Sections start on the headline itself.

Don't lead persuasive surfaces with a centred SaaS hero, a grid of identical cards or a network-constellation hero. Graph structure appears as a small labelled neighbourhood of at most eight nodes inside the Why panel.
